Your calls. Your voice. Your shield.
Sparta helps you decide which calls reach you. On this phone it can silence the ringer for unknown callers, reject numbers you blocked, and tell you what it did.
Honest by design
When Sparta talks to a caller (only when a call reaches your Sparta telephony number), it always says it is an AI assistant. It never pretends to be you, and it never records calls.
Sparta cannot answer an ordinary phone call on this phone or hear its audio. Android does not allow that.
Connect your Sparta backend
The backend keeps your history and block lists, and runs the analysis. You can skip this: screening on this phone still works with local settings, but nothing syncs.

Let Sparta screen your calls

Android lets one app at a time be your call-screening app. If you choose Sparta, Android asks it about each incoming call and Sparta can let it ring, silence the ringer, or reject it. It cannot answer the call or hear what is said.

Optional permissions
Both permissions are optional. Sparta asks only when you press a button here, and explains first.
Notifications
Sparta uses notifications to tell you when a call needs your decision and when it silenced or blocked a caller. Without them you only see decisions inside the app.
Allow notifications

Saved contacts as known callers

If you turn this on, Sparta checks whether an incoming number is in your contacts and lets those calls ring. It only asks Android a yes or no question about the number; it does not read, copy or upload your contacts.
Treat saved contacts as known callers

Optional: live AI audio needs forwarding

An AI conversation with a caller only happens when the call reaches your Sparta telephony number. On a normal phone line that means asking your carrier to forward unanswered calls to that number. Screening on this phone works without it.
